questions: Is line_loss_events 0 on s-bend and slalom at y=0.07 m with the +/-0.065 m spread? If not, which track and at what max_error?
Does slalom max_error fall below 0.06 m with this spread? Report the value per track.
Does s-bend progress return to about 0.14 to 0.155, or does it fall back toward 0.04 as in iteration 7?
Does slalom steering_oscillation fall below 0.10? If not, lead and speed are not its cause and the controller is the next lever.
Does the oval still stop at progress 0.115 with max_error near 0.061 m? If so, confirm that spread and row position do not affect it.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If line loss returns on s-bend or slalom at y=0.07 m with the +/-0.065 m spread, the spread is the likely trigger, so revert to the +/-0.05 m spread with y=0.07 m (iteration 3 layout). If line loss is 0 and slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m, widen the spread to +/-0.08 m with 16 mm footprints.

intent: Restore the sensor row to y=0.07 m, the best-scoring lead (iteration 3, 51.31), while keeping the wider +/-0.065 m spread and 16 mm footprints. Change only the row position from iteration 7, so the result shows whether the slalom line loss came from the 0.065 m lead or from the spread. Ground speed stays at wheel_radius 0.03 m, because 0.04 m caused line loss in iteration 6.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that y=0.065 m with the wider spread did not hold the line on slalom and gave s-bend progress of 0.04. The s-bend lead gain seems to need the 0.07 m row. Slalom steering_oscillation has stayed near 0.13 to 0.14 at every row position tested (y=0.05 to 0.07 m), so it is probably not a geometry problem. Next I need to know whether the wider spread alone keeps the line at the 0.07 m lead, which decides whether the spread or the lead caused the iteration 7 slalom line loss.
rationale: Iteration 7 (y=0.065 m, +/-0.065 m spread, 16 mm, radius 0.03 m) scored 35.77, below iteration 3 (51.31). Slalom line loss returned at one event per run, slalom steering_oscillation stayed at 0.134, and s-bend progress fell back to 0.04. Its slalom max_error was 0.0642 m. The s-bend result matched the iteration 0 to 2 values exactly, and iteration 4's s-bend range (15.43 to 73.47) shows that seed variance is large. The Integrator's stated rule applies: if line loss returns at sensor y=0.065 m with the wider spread, return the row to y=0.07 m and keep the +/-0.065 m spread. That rule is consistent with the evidence, because the best score came from the y=0.07 m row and speed at 0.03 m, and iteration 6 showed that speed 0.04 m also causes line loss. I therefore change only the sensor row, from y=0.065 m back to y=0.07 m. The +/-0.065 m spread, 16 mm footprints, body, mass, wheel track and wheel radius stay fixed. This isolates the lead effect against iteration 7 and tests whether the wider spread alone can hold the line at y=0.07 m. Expected result: s-bend progress near 0.14 to 0.155, slalom max_error below about 0.06 m, and a score near or above 51 if line loss does not return. Risk: the wider spread may not stop the slalom line loss at y=0.07 m, which would point to the lead, not the spread, as the trigger.
